title: The Crow and the Pitcher
summary: A thirsty person finds a deep water pot and tries to reach the water.
coverScene: A clever crow dropping small stones into a tall glass pitcher filled with water.

sentences.text: One hot summer day, a very dry bird flew across the dry land to find some water.
After a long search, he discovered a tall vessel that had a little liquid at the bottom.
The animal was extremely happy because he hoped to drink and feel better.
However, a big problem appeared when he tried to reach the liquid.
The neck of the container was too narrow, and the water level was much too low for his face.
He tried to push his head inside, but he could not touch the cool drink.
Many birds would have given up and left the place in silence.
This smart bird, who had a very strong mind, refused to stop.
Instead of walking away, he stood quiet and began to think about how he could solve the difficulty.
Soon, his bright eyes saw some small stones on the ground near the grass.
An idea came to him which would change the situation completely.
He picked up a stone one by one in his mouth and carried it carefully toward the pitcher.
With great care, the bird dropped the small rocks into the open top of the glass.
As each piece fell down into the bottom, the liquid started to rise higher and higher.
The smart animal continued this work until the water reached the top.
Finally, the bird was able to drink easily and satisfy his terrible need.

sentences.text: Beneath the merciless glare of a midsummer sky, a solitary corvid traversed a landscape stripped of its vitality by the relentless heat.
The terrain stretched out before him in dusty shades of ochre and bone, offering neither shade nor respite from the stifling atmosphere.
His throat burned with a fierce, desiccated ache that turned every beat of his wings into an exertion of sheer will.
For hours, he had scavenged the parched earth, driven solely by the primal imperative to find moisture or perish.
It was precisely when despair threatened to anchor his wings that his sharp eyes caught a faint glint of ceramic rising from the dirt ahead.
Approaching swiftly, he discovered a tall, narrow-necked vessel standing half-buried near the withered remnants of a forgotten garden.
With a surge of anticipation that fluttered wildly in his chest, he peered over the rim and perceived a tiny pool of liquid shimmering at the bottom.
The sight momentarily cured his exhaustion, filling his mind with the vivid promise of cool, life-giving water.
Yet, no sooner had the hope bloomed than it was crushed by a cruel physical reality.
The neck of the container was frustratingly slender, and the water level sat far below the reach of his eager beak.
He thrust his head downward, straining every muscle in his neck, but his skull met the unyielding clay wall long before his tongue could graze the surface.
Again and again, he angled his body, twisting and stretching in desperate attempts to bridge the impossible gap between desire and fulfillment.
The cool liquid mocked him with its silent presence, just inches beyond his grasp yet functionally as distant as the clouds.
An ordinary creature of the wild would surely have surrendered to the tyranny of circumstance, turning away to accept a bleak fate in the dust.
Not so this bird, whose intellect burned brighter than the sun overhead and refused to yield to an obvious defeat.
Standing perfectly still upon the sun-baked soil, he fixed his intelligent gaze upon the obstacle and began to dissect the problem with methodical precision.
Random exertion had failed, which meant that only careful strategy could alter the immutable laws of the container.
As his sharp eyes scanned the immediate surroundings, they fell upon a scattering of small, heavy pebbles half-embedded in the dry earth near a tuft of grass.
A sudden spark of insight illuminated his thoughts, bridging the gap between what was and what could be.
He realized that if the water could not rise to meet him, he would have to force the water to ascend by displacing the empty space it occupied.
Moving with deliberate care, he hopped over to the nearest stone and grasped it firmly within his dark beak.
The pebble was surprisingly heavy, taxing his strength as he carried it back across the dirt toward the mouth of the tall pitcher.
With meticulous precision, he dropped the small rock into the narrow opening, listening intently as it fell through the darkness.
A dull, echoing splash signaled its arrival at the bottom, though the water level appeared frustratingly unchanged by the tiny addition.
Undeterred by the microscopic margin of progress, the bird immediately turned back toward the grass to secure another piece.
Slowly, relentlessly, the arduous labor continued beneath the scorching afternoon heat.
He picked up a third stone, carried it forward with aching muscles, and released it into the waiting vessel.
With every single rock that tumbled into the depths, the displaced liquid crept upward by a fraction of a millimeter.
Other animals might have abandoned such tedious work long before, but this bird understood that cumulative effort is the truest weapon against insurmountable odds.
His bright eyes remained locked on the opening, measuring the minuscule gains that collectively spelled the difference between life and death.
The sun traced its slow arc across the sky, casting lengthening shadows over the dry land while the solitary worker maintained his steady rhythm.
No matter how weary his wings felt or how dry his throat became, he refused to allow impatience to disrupt his methodical task.
The pile of stones upon the ground dwindled as the invisible column of water inside the pitcher inched ever closer to the rim.
He watched the liquid rise with a triumphant flutter in his breast, knowing that his intellectual persistence was finally bearing fruit.
Every single action mattered in this grand design, proving that reason could conquer physical barriers that brute force could never dismantle.
At last, after what felt like an eternity of patient labor, the shining surface of the water crested near the top of the narrow neck.
He peered inside and saw the cool, sweet liquid waiting right beneath the opening, entirely within his reach.
With a profound sense of accomplishment, he lowered his beak and drank deeply, soothing the burning agony in his throat until his thirst was fully quenched.
His strength rushed back into his limbs, replacing the exhaustion of the long afternoon with the vibrant energy of survival.
This remarkable event stood as undeniable proof that careful thought and unwavering perseverance can overcome even the most daunting adversities.
Humanity has passed down this tale through countless generations because it captures a fundamental truth about existence.
When people encounter massive walls in their daily lives, they are often tempted to surrender to despair.
Yet the clever bird teaches us that no problem is truly absolute if one approaches it with a calm mind and a willingness to break a challenge into manageable parts.
Small steps taken consistently can lead to monumental achievements over time, just as tiny pebbles raised the water in the pitcher.
The world is full of challenges that demand deep thought rather than reckless action, rewarding those who refuse to let fear dictate their limits.
Teachers share this narrative with young minds in schools everywhere, ensuring that the lesson of the clever corvid endures across time.
Children and adults alike find inspiration in the sight of a small creature outsmarting a harsh environment through pure reason.
Every single day brings new chances to improve our circumstances, provided we possess the patience to work steadily toward our goals.
By keeping a clear head during difficult moments, we unlock the hidden potential to alter our futures for the better.
Let us remember this timeless example whenever we face adversity, knowing that success belongs to those who think deeply and act with quiet determination.
